briefdescription.para: The type with which an expression stores an operand.

detaileddescription.para: Applied by the deduction guides and the factory functions to the type deduced for a forwarding reference: X& (or const X&) for an lvalue, X for an rvalue.

An lvalue is copied into the expression, so that an expression built in a function from its parameters, and returned, does not refer to the destroyed locals of that function. An rvalue is moved into the expression, so that an expression that outlives the statement, like auto op = eq (f (), 1);, does not refer to a destroyed temporary.

The arrays and the character pointers are first converted by as_operand() to basic_c_string or array_operand, which are stored, but which refer to the characters or to the elements of the operand, without copying them; such an expression is valid only as long as the operand.

Only an lvalue of a class type that cannot be copied (for example a std::unique_ptr) is stored as a const reference; such a reference remains valid only as long as the named operand, which is always the case within the statement that checks the expression.

briefdescription.para: Appends the shortest decimal representation of a numeric value to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para:
T
The numeric type to format.
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The value to format.
Returns
Nothing.
The value is formatted into a local buffer, which is then appended to buffer.

For long double, a platform-specific path is chosen:
On Windows and on platforms where long double has the same storage width as double (e.g. 32-bit Arm), the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars.
On all other platforms (e.g. x86-64 Linux/macOS with 80-bit extended precision, or AArch64 and RISC-V with 128-bit quad precision), snprintf with %.*Lg is used as a portable fallback, because std::to_chars for long double may be unavailable (e.g. when linking with lld). The precision starts at LDBL_DIG and is increased until the text reads back, with strtold, as the same value, up to LDBL_DECIMAL_DIG, which always reads back exactly. This gives the shortest exact form, as std::to_chars gives for the other types; a shorter form would need fewer than LDBL_DIG digits, and Lg removes the trailing zeros, so starting at LDBL_DIG does not lose it. For zero and the subnormal values, which have fewer significant digits, the precision starts at 1. The value of errno, which strtold may set for subnormal values, is preserved. If no precision reads back exactly, the C library handles long double with the precision of double (e.g. newlib on AArch64 and RISC-V), and the value is cast to double and formatted with std::to_chars, as above.

For all other numeric types, std::to_chars is called directly, providing locale-independent formatting. The snprintf() path uses the decimal point of the C locale, which is . unless the application changes it with setlocale().

briefdescription.para: Appends the hexadecimal address of a pointer to a buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Shared by the reporter and the expression_formatter, so that the pointers are displayed identically in the messages and in the expressions. Pointers to const or volatile objects, and function pointers, are accepted too.

T
The type pointed to (an object or a function type).
buffer
The string to append to.
v
The pointer.
Returns
Nothing.
Null pointers are rendered as "0x0", regardless of the platform, avoiding platform-specific representations such as "(nil)" on Linux/glibc. Non-null pointers are formatted with snprintf(), using the p specifier.

The p specifier expects a void*. Object pointers are converted implicitly to const volatile void*, which accepts any qualification, and the qualifiers are then removed with const_cast; a reinterpret_cast to void* would not compile for pointers to const objects. The object is not accessed. Function pointers, which do not convert to void* implicitly, use reinterpret_cast.

detaileddescription.para: Without additional arguments, the callable already has the signature void (Self_T&), and a copy of it is returned, without a wrapper.

Otherwise, a bound_callable stores copies of the callable and of the arguments (decayed, as by auto), since a suite may run after the caller's temporaries are gone; the callable receives the copies as non-const lvalues. A reference parameter thus refers to the copy; to refer to the caller's object, pass a pointer, or std::ref(), which converts to a T& parameter (an auto& parameter receives the std::reference_wrapper itself).

The returned object holds a copy of the callable (decayed, as by auto) when there are no additional arguments; otherwise it is a bound_callable that holds copies of the callable and of the arguments, and passes the arguments after the leading reference, which is passed when the body is invoked. A suite stores the object in a std::function, since it runs later; a test case, which runs immediately, refers to it with a callable_ref.

briefdescription.para: Tells whether two numbers differ by at most a tolerance.

detaileddescription.para: If the three values are integers, the distance is computed exactly, as an unsigned value, also for operands of mixed signedness, and compared with the tolerance with std::cmp_less_equal(), so that neither overflows nor wraps around. Otherwise, the values are converted to their common floating-point type, and the absolute value of the difference is compared with the tolerance. A negative tolerance, or a NaN, makes the result false.

Lhs_T
The arithmetic type of the first value.
Rhs_T
The arithmetic type of the second value.
Epsilon_T
The arithmetic type of the tolerance.
lhs
The first value.
rhs
The second value.
epsilon
The tolerance.
true
The distance between the values is less than or equal to the tolerance.
false
Otherwise.
For the integers, the larger value is selected with std::cmp_less(), and the distance is computed in std::uintmax_t: when both values have the same sign, as the modular difference of their conversions, which is exact; otherwise, as the sum of the larger value and of the magnitude of the negative one. A sum that does not fit in std::uintmax_t is flagged as an overflow, and gives false, since the true distance is larger than any tolerance. The tolerance is compared with std::cmp_less_equal(), so a negative one gives false.

For the other types, the values are converted to their common type, which is a floating-point one, so std::int64_t values compared with a float tolerance lose precision; the comparison is inclusive, so a distance equal to the tolerance succeeds. Two equal values, including two infinities of the same sign, whose difference would be NaN, are at the distance zero; a NaN operand always fails.

briefdescription.para: Internal implementation details for the µTest++ framework.

detaileddescription.para: The detail namespace encapsulates the internal mechanisms, helper structures, and implementation utilities employed by the µTest++ testing framework. These components do not form part of the public API and may be modified without prior notice.

Within this namespace, one will find the deprecated value wrappers (declared in deprecated.h), the value unwrapping helper, comparator structures for logical and relational operations, mechanisms for exception checking, the reporters, the check result, and the expression formatter.
All definitions within detail are intended exclusively for internal use; the applications do not need to name them.
